what: Bank of Montreal is one of Canada's big six banks. It serves Canadian households and businesses, owns a large US retail bank across the Midwest after buying Bank of the West, and runs capital markets and wealth management.
customers: Canadian and US retail customers, small businesses, corporations and institutional investors.
money: Canadian deposits, mortgages and business lending
Midwestern US retail and commercial banking
moat: An oligopoly position in Canadian banking where six banks hold most deposits, plus a large US franchise that few Canadian banks have built.
risks: Canadian household debt is high relative to income
US commercial lending losses rose after the Bank of the West purchase
Canadian housing is sensitive to mortgage renewal at higher rates
Analyst price targets imply little upside at current levels
opportunities: Revenue grew about 10% last year as margins recovered
The US business gives growth that Canada alone cannot provide
A dividend that has been paid without interruption since 1829
watch: US commercial credit losses and Canadian mortgage renewal performance.
